content:
Hi all! Wojciech's wishlist mentions that the goal diff is coarse (#general > Wojciech's Widget Wishlist @ 💬). I am working with iris-lean, and found that the goal-diff misbehaves for its proof mode, as well as for Std.Do's. Consider the following example:

import Std.Tactic.Do
open Std.Do

example (P Q R S : Prop) : (P → Q) → P → R → S → Q := by
  intro HPQ HP HR HS
  specialize HPQ HP
  exact HPQ

example (P Q R S : SPred [Nat]) : ⊢ₛ (P → Q) → P → R → S → Q := by
  mintro HPQ HP HR HS
  mspecialize HPQ HP
  mexact HPQ

proof diff view for specialize:

proof diff view for mspecialize:

With ordinary hypotheses, specialize highlights just the consumed premise. With mspecialize, every hypothesis the step didn't touch (HP, HR, HS) is highlighted both before and after, while HPQ, the one that changes, isn't highlighted before the step.

The cause is that the proof mode, like iris-lean, stores its hypotheses inside the goal term: MGoalEntails σs (H₁ ∧ H₂ ∧ …) target, with names in mdata. exprDiffCore compares subexpressions positionally, so once a tactic adds, removes or reorders a hypothesis, the remaining hypotheses can end up being compared against the wrong ones. This also affects similar proof modes like Lentil (https://github.com/verse-lab/Lentil)

Each of these proof modes gives its hypotheses a stable identity, so the diff could align hypotheses by it before comparing them, just as diffHypothesesBundle does by fvar (I tried this out in a quick prototype). 

Would you take an extension point for this in core? For example @[goal_diff Std.Do.MGoalEntails], where each proof mode could suppy the diff for its own goal form, with exprDiff as the fallback. This would need ExprDiff/exprDiff/addDiffTags to be public again. I’m also happy to go a different route if you’d prefer another mechanism.

If this sounds reasonable, I’m happy to write the PR.

@Sebastian Graf, since this affects Std.Do: would such a hook be useful there too?

@Klaus Kraßnitzer thank you for reporting this issue! The set of ordinary hypotheses is diffed as a name->type dictionary. As you observe, this is not the case for hypotheses appearing in entailment relations - they are diffed as part of the goal Expr which doesn't give the right output.

The proposed solution is not the right one here, however. The basic underlying issue is that custom proof modes can't display their entailments as custom tactic states - the tactic state display is not customizable. If it were, these proof modes could reuse the diff mechanism as part of their display function. We should prefer this approach since it is more extensible than only customizing the diffs.

Ah, that makes sense, thanks! I agree that making the tactic state display extensible would be a much nicer and more general solution.

Is there already a design or existing work towards making this customizable? I'd be interested in looking into it, although I imagine the scope would be quite a bit larger than the goal-diff hook I had in mind.

The builtin display can't be customized, but you can define and render your own display alongside it. I pushed a commit to demonstrate how that might work with ProofWidgets components. Warning: entirely vibe-coded, and we can see some immediate issues with it:

  • The builtin display cannot be hidden, so we see both the builtin display and our custom display. (We could actually hide it with a hack: find the appropriate DOM element via JS and set display: none.)
  • The components and utility functions that make up the builtin display - which would be convenient for custom displays to reuse - are not exported from the @leanprover/infoview package, so end up copy-pasted into tacticState.tsx.
  • Setting the selected hypotheses (shift-click) is not accessible to user widgets, so the custom tactic state selection doesn't interact with the builtin one. Some other functionality is also missing.

Fixing these things, or providing a more tailored custom-tactic-state API, is unfortunately not on the immediate roadmap.

BUT it mostly works; you can already write your own tactic state, if you are willing to tolerate some ugly code.
